title: A letter from Rome to Alexandria, AD 50
intro: Two engines in a chain. A map finds the fastest way from Rome to Alexandria for the month of departure: across the open sea from April to October, along the coasts when the sea is “closed” (mare clausum). A chronology then turns the journey into dates: it counts the days from the Julian date of departure and says when the letter arrives, in the Julian calendar, in years from the founding of Rome (AUC) and in the Roman way of counting days before the Kalends, Nones or Ides. Pick the day of departure and the speed of the ships.
aucLabel: Arrival: year from the founding of Rome (AUC, Varro)
romCountLabel: Arrival: day counted before the next Kalends, Nones or Ides (inclusive)
mapTitle: The fastest route on a Lambert conformal conic map
chartTitle: Departure and arrival on a time line (Julian calendar)
